tx:
• After completion of The Elder Kiln, players can sacrifice their fire cape to TokHaar-Hok in the Fight Kiln to gain permanent access to the Fight Kiln minigame, which is a more difficult version of the TzHaar Fight Cave. Sacrificing a fire cape only needs to be done once. After completing the Fight Kiln, players can choose to receive a more powerful cape, one of the TokHaar-Kal variants.
• The fire cape is normally required to fight ice strykewyrms. A TokHaar-Kal or Igneous Kal will also count as a fire cape for this purpose. This requirement can be bypassed by paying 2,000 Slayer points to unlock the ability to fight the ice strykewyrms without needing the cape. Without the unlock or the cape, the ice strykewyrms can't be assigned as a slayer task. When worn, the fire cape has a bonus effect that increases all damage dealt by fire spells to ice strykewyrms.
• This item is also used in a master emote clue step in conjunction with a toktz-ket-xil and a spork, where the player needs to cheer by the sulphur pit of the TzHaar City. There is a hidey-hole near to the sulphur pit allowing the player to store the cape. In order to build it, you must have 88 Construction. It requires 4 mahogany planks, 10 steel nails, and 1 gold leaf.
• Players can sell it to TzHaar-Mej-Jal for 8,000 tokkul.

Shard of Genesis Essence can be used to unlock an "Innate Mastery" enchantment for tier 95 weapons. When wielding a weapon upgraded by the shard, player's damage and accuracy are increased to values of a tier 100 weapon. One shard is required for upgrading a two-handed weapon or a dual-wield weapon set.
The weapon must be used on the shard; using the shard on the weapon does not work. For dual-wielded weapon sets, it is not required to own both weapons in order to unlock the effect for that set, and either the main-hand or the off-hand can be used on the Shard of Genesis Essence to do so.
A total of 9 Shards of Genesis Essence are required to unlock all available upgrades:
The upgrade is permanently bound to the character, not to specific weapons themselves; every relevant weapon (or dual-wielded set) will have the effect, including those that are received, created, or purchased afterwards.
